description: FIND-203's fix specifies `evaluateColdStartKillSwitch` as the concrete mechanism enforcing REQ-105's binding pause SHALL, and REQ-106's own Edge Cases/Acceptance Criteria (lines 853-856, 666-670) state it must be 'called by REQ-106's issuance step BEFORE acquiring the loan_${lenderId} lock.' However, re-reading verification-architecture.md's full 48-item Proof Obligations table confirms there is NO Tier-0 structural proof obligation anywhere requiring the REAL, production REQ-106 issuance implementation to actually invoke this function. The ONLY proof obligation covering it is PROP-105g (Tier 1, i.e. a pure-function unit test), whose own stated test method is: 'unit test, fixed fixtures: {sampleSize:10,rate:0.7,defaultedCount:3}->{paused:true} ...; PLUS an integration-style fixture wiring the paused:true output into a MOCKED REQ-106 issuance call, asserting refusal before the lock is ever acquired.' A test that wires a function's output into a MOCKED caller proves only that IF the real issuance code follows this wiring pattern, the desired behavior results -- it does NOT, and structurally cannot, prove the REAL REQ-106 issuance implementation ever calls evaluateColdStartKillSwitch at all. This is a materially weaker verification method than this SAME requirement uses for its OTHER similarly load-bearing wiring facts: PROP-106d (Tier 0, 'structural/Tier-0 check: source-grep or import-identity check across the diff confirming a single import site') and PROP-106i (Tier 0, 'structural/Tier-0 check: source-grep/read of REQ-106's own issuance critical section confirming it references ONLY loan_${lenderId} as its lock key') both demand a real read of the ACTUAL production source. No analogous Tier-0 check exists for the kill-switch call site. Gate item (2) in verification-architecture.md (lines 206-219) likewise only demands confirmation 'via evaluateColdStartKillSwitch... correctly pausing at sampleSize>=10 AND rate<0.80 OR... (PROP-105g)' -- i.e. it cites the SAME Tier-1/mocked-Tier-2 proof obligation as its complete verification method, never a control-flow read of REQ-106's real issuance code confirming the call site exists. As specified, an implementation could pass every stated proof obligation in this document while the real, production loan-issuance function never calls evaluateColdStartKillSwitch at all for a genuine cold-start request -- precisely 'a computed flag nobody checks,' the exact failure mode the manifest specifically asks this review to rule out, and precisely the class of gap FIND-203 was meant to close (a SHALL with zero backing proof obligation) but has only partially closed (a SHALL with a proof obligation that tests the function in isolation and via a mock, never the real wiring).

evidence.snippet: PROP-105g | REQ-105 | evaluateColdStartKillSwitch(...) correctly implements the kill-switch's own binding pause rule ... | 1 | true | unit test, fixed fixtures: ... PLUS an integration-style fixture wiring the paused:true output into a mocked REQ-106 issuance call, asserting refusal before the lock is ever acquired

crossCheck.note: Contrast PROP-106d ('structural/Tier-0 check: source-grep or import-identity check across the diff confirming a single import site and zero hardcoded loans.jsonl path strings elsewhere') and PROP-106i ('structural/Tier-0 check: source-grep/read of REQ-106's own issuance critical section confirming it references ONLY loan_${lenderId} as its lock key') -- both Tier 0, both demanding a read of the REAL implementation. No equivalent Tier-0 entry exists anywhere in the 48-item table for confirming the real REQ-106 issuance code path actually calls evaluateColdStartKillSwitch before disbursing a cold-start loan.
